page.title: What Is a Variable in Python?
page.introduction: Before working with functions, classes, data structures, and other Python concepts, it is important to understand how variables work and how Python associates names with objects.
page.definition: A variable in Python is a name that refers to an object stored in memory.

explanation.content: When Python executes x = 10, the name x becomes associated with an integer object representing the value 10.
A Python variable is therefore better understood as a name binding or reference rather than a box that directly contains a value.
This model becomes especially important when multiple variables refer to the same object or when a variable is reassigned to a different object.

analogy.title: A Label Attached to a Storage Box
analogy.description: Imagine a storage room containing many boxes. Instead of writing the entire contents of a box every time you want to find it, you give the box a meaningful label such as “Books” or “Documents”. The label helps you identify and access the box, while the actual contents remain inside the box.
analogy.connection: In Python, the variable name works like the label. The object is like the box and its contents. When you write x = 10, the name x becomes associated with the integer object representing 10.

page.takeaway: Think of a Python variable as a name or label associated with an object. The name and the object are separate concepts: the name provides a way to refer to the object.
